ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and its first two limbs fail on the driver's own trace. The trace carries 79 driver fixes and not one of them is a qualifying in-geofence fix: qualifying_fix_count is 0, and the closest the driver ever came to the pickup pin across the whole trip was a minimum distance of 448.97 m. The arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup is 120 m, so the driver was never inside the pickup geofence at all — more than three and a half radii away at his nearest approach. Limb (b), which requires the gps_trace to place him inside the geofence at or before the 'arrived' event, therefore fails, and with it the whole charge.

Limb (c) fails as arithmetic. The minimum dwell for a LARGE_VENUE pickup is 300 seconds, and the longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run in this trace is 0.0 seconds — there is no qualifying run at all: fix_count 0, first_ts null, last_ts null. The driver cannot satisfy a 300 second continuous in-geofence dwell when he was never in the geofence for a single fix, let alone a run of them.

Limb (d) fails on a field the platform wrote itself. The clause requires the trip_record to show the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The record shows cancelled_by 'SYSTEM' and cancellation_reason_code 'SYSTEM_TIMEOUT' at 23:23:40 — a system timeout, not a driver termination, and none of the three recognised codes. There is no driver-asserted rider no-show anywhere in this record, only the platform's own clock expiring.

POL-NS-02 gives the rider an outright entitlement on these facts. Across the entire trace, and therefore across the whole 15 minutes preceding the 23:23:40 cancellation, there is no qualifying in-radius fix at any point. The test is not 'roughly where was he' — it is whether fixes at 25 m accuracy or better fell inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE radius, and none did. The driver is accordingly deemed never to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the fee, because its 400 m ceiling is not met. That clause governs only a driver who was stationary for the required dwell outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin. This driver's minimum distance from the pin was 448.97 m and his mean was 806.56 m, with a maximum of 1,629.10 m. He was never within the ceiling, so there is no wrong-entrance or wrong-face case to allocate, and no gateway to driver compensation.

The 'arrived' marker at 23:15:20 is false under POL-NS-05 on either of its independent triggers. First, at that timestamp the driver's position was at least 448.97 m from the pin — his trace minimum — which is over the 300 m threshold. Second, every distinct speed in his trace (43 values from 23.3 to 39.0 km/h, none of them zero) is above the 15 km/h motion threshold, so he was still driving, not waiting. Under POL-NS-05(ii), where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. His account that there was 'no parking so I circled' describes driving, and the trace shows nothing but driving.

POL-NS-06 states the shortfall directly, and the numbers should be stated: the minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup is 300 seconds, the measured effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds, and the shortfall is 300.0 seconds. The cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The driver let the trip time out with the entire statutory waiting period still unserved.

The driver's only excuse for the shortfall — 'no parking so I circled' — is the limb (i) argument, and limb (i) is unavailable on this record. It requires a traffic_advisory whose geometry covers the pickup road, whose active window covers the waiting period, and whose type is KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-00606-01 is MISSING: it has no payload, its only issue is MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING), and it carries weight_multiplier 0.0. I disclose that impairment and cite the absence itself: no advisory covers this road, and a MISSING advisory makes limb (i) unavailable rather than exonerating the driver. Limb (i)'s second condition fails independently in any event — the driver was never within the 300 m leash, let alone inside the geofence, so there is no out-and-back interval to accumulate.

The rider did everything the platform asks of her and the trace proves it. Her track runs from 23:14:40 to 23:23:40 with 61 fixes, and all 61 qualify: a stationary device (single distinct speed of 0.0 km/h) between 7.90 m and 17.08 m from the pin, mean 12.85 m. That is well inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, and it is the majority — in fact the entirety — of the qualifying fixes across the waiting window. She was at the pin, alone, at 11 pm, while the driver's trace places him between 449 m and 1.63 km away.

The driver's chat conduct meets POL-NS-04(b), and the exchange shows who moved to end the trip. The driver opened it himself at 23:16:30 with 'car problem, you cancel' — he asked the rider to cancel rather than wait for her — and when she answered at 23:16:40 he posted no reply at all; the export ends there, over seven minutes before the system cancelled. He placed no in-app voice call either: the only entry in trip_record.in_app_calls is the rider's own call at 23:15:40, answered for 40 seconds. I do not overstate limb (a): the rider's single message 'no, you cancel' is a coordination message within the exchange the driver opened, and whether the judge reads it as inside the clause's enumerated list is the narrower question. The refund does not depend on it, because POL-NS-01 fails outright, POL-NS-02 applies, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full regardless.

Nothing here requires escalation, and escalation would leave the rider worse off: it holds the fee rather than refunding it and issues no monetary ruling. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issues, so there is no POL-NS-09(a) or POL-NS-09(e) trigger. The only apparent conflict — the trip_record's 23:15:20 'arrived' event and 8.3 minute wait against a trace that never enters the geofence — is not a POL-NS-09(b) conflict, because POL-NS-05 exists precisely to resolve it by recomputing the waiting clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix. There is no clock skew under POL-NS-08(a) either: the arrival event lands squarely on the trace's 10 second fix cadence, and the sampling has no gaps at all (max_gap_sec 0.0, coverage 100%). On the profile counters, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides, so POL-NS-09(c) and POL-NS-09(d) do not fire; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip either (1 no-show termination against the 4 the clause requires, over 110 completed trips).

On quantum, the contested amount is the SGD 6.00 cancellation-fee line, which is charged and not refunded (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0). I do not contend the arithmetic of the line is wrong — 6.00 is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (6.00), so the fare reconciles with the fee_schedule resolution rule and there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect — but a fee that is unchargeable in principle does not become chargeable because it was computed correctly. The whole 6.00 line returns to the rider as a FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03, with no driver compensation payable.

The SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is the correct amount for this trip and reconciles with the fee schedule. Under the resolution rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the zone-class fee (LARGE_VENUE, SGD 4.00) and the vehicle-tier fee (RYDE_PLUS, SGD 6.00), and the ledger line carries exactly SGD 6.00, with base fare, distance fare, time fare, platform fee and promo all at zero - nothing is stacked on top. There is therefore no fare defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) describes, and no arithmetic basis on which any part of this charge could be trimmed.

On the platform's own trip record the driver marked arrival at 23:15:20 and the trip was still running at 23:23:40, when the SYSTEM timed it out - a recorded waiting period of 8.3 minutes. That is well past the 300-second minimum dwell that POL-NS-01(c) fixes for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The driver also never cancelled the trip himself: the termination is recorded as SYSTEM_TIMEOUT with cancelled_by SYSTEM, so he did not abandon the pickup or walk away from the assignment.

Nothing in the driver's profile withholds his compensation. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND that count divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d above 0.08; here the count is 1 and the rate is 1/110 = 0.009, so neither limb is met, compensation is not withheld and the escalation branch is not reached. On the ledger arithmetic the driver's share of the SGD 6.00 fee is SGD 4.80 at the 80 percent rate. For the same reason the driver-side abuse limb of POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged.

Two admissible artifacts at full weight cannot both be true about this pickup. The trip record asserts an arrival marker at 23:15:20 and an 8.3-minute wait; the GPS trace never places the driver closer than 448.97 m to the pin, shows him in continuous motion between 23.3 and 39.0 kph across all 79 fixes, and yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds. Neither artifact is impaired - both are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - and the platform's own two records are in direct conflict on arrival and dwell. That is the situation POL-NS-09(b) reserves for a human reviewer, and escalation holds the disputed SGD 6.00 rather than refunding it, which is the right disposition while it is worked out which of the platform's own two records is wrong.

The rider cannot take the POL-NS-04 route out of this fee. Limb (a) requires a message whose content is locating or coordinating - the rider's own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that she cannot see the vehicle. The only message she sent was 'no, you cancel' at 23:16:40, which is none of those things; on this record she never named an entrance, block or her own position at the Clarke Quay pickup, so the coordination failure POL-NS-04 is written to address is not made out.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01, which requires all four of its conditions together. The driver's 'arrived' event is recorded at 23:15:20 in the trip record (EV-TRIP-00606), but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00606 — 79 driver fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps) never places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE pickup geofence. His closest approach to the pin was 448.97 m, his mean distance 806.56 m and his furthest 1,629.10 m; the trace yields 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds. Condition (b) therefore fails, and condition (c) fails as arithmetic: effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. Condition (d) also fails — the trip was ended by the platform, not the driver (cancelled_by SYSTEM, cancellation_reason_code SYSTEM_TIMEOUT at 23:23:40), which is none of RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT.

The driver's argument that the trip record shows an 8.3-minute wait (payload.wait_time_min) past the 300-second minimum is rejected: POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap, and there were no qualifying in-geofence fixes at all. His argument that he did not abandon the pickup because the SYSTEM timed it out is also rejected — a system timeout is precisely what limb (d) does not recognise. I accept his point that no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists: SGD 6.00 is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_PLUS vehicle-tier fee (SGD 6.00), so the ledger line reconciles with the fee schedule. That does not make an unchargeable fee chargeable.

The arrival marker is false under POL-NS-05 on both of its independent triggers: at 23:15:20 the driver was more than 300 m from the pin, and every one of the 43 distinct speeds in his trace (23.3–39.0 km/h) is above the 15 km/h threshold — he was driving, not waiting. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) gives the rider the full SGD 6.00 refund and expressly excludes driver compensation; POL-NS-06 independently refunds the same SGD 6.00 for the 300.0-second shortfall, and its limb (i) cannot rescue the driver because EV-ADVIS-00606-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING), so no advisory permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed.

POL-NS-03 does not apply: it governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and this driver was never closer than 448.97 m and never stationary. POL-NS-04 does not need to be reached — the rider's single message, 'no, you cancel', is not one of the locating or coordinating messages limb (a) lists, so that route is not made out — but the refund does not depend on it, and the rider's track (61 fixes, all qualifying, stationary, 7.90–17.08 m from the pin, inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE presence radius) is consistent with her account that she was waiting at the pin.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-06 each expressly exclude compensation. The anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination in 30 days against the 4 required; 1/110 = 0.009 against the 0.08 rate), but that is not what withholds payment here.

No escalation. The apparent conflict between the trip record's arrival event and the GPS trace is exactly what POL-NS-05 resolves by recomputing the waiting clock, so POL-NS-09(b) is not engaged. There is no POL-NS-08 impairment on any limb: no clock skew (the arrival event lands on the 10-second fix cadence and trace start/end match the trip record to the second), no trace gap (max_gap_sec 0.0), chat message count matches the trip record (2), and the fee reconciles. POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire — both counterparty-dispute counters are 0 and the anti-farming check is clear. The deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no discount applies.

One referral rides with this ruling, produced by POL-NS-05(ii) itself and not by any request of mine.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii) — record a false-arrival event against driver DRV-30640 for trip TRP-00606 (arrival marker set at 23:15:20 while the driver was 448.97 m from the pin and moving at 23.3–39.0 km/h, and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip).
